nodes.title: SG-5.4.1 planPreload and resolveTextureKey engine functions
nodes.body:
Context: a search of game/ for planPreload and resolveTextureKey returns nothing. The manifest loader (game/src/assets/loaders/manifestLoader.ts) already exports FALLBACK_ASSET_ID and checkAssetRefs. Desired behavior: a pure planPreload dedupes the asset ids a scene references and reports unknown references, and a pure resolveTextureKey returns the fallback asset id for unknown ids. Expected result: both functions are importable from game/src/engine. Why: the asset preload step (SG-5.4) needs them.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a scene that references the same asset id more than once, when planPreload runs, then each known id appears once in the plan.
- Given a scene that references an id that is not in the manifest, when planPreload runs, then that id is reported as unknown.
- Given an id that is not in the manifest, when resolveTextureKey runs, then it returns the fallback asset id.


## Scope
- In scope: New pure engine module game/src/engine/planPreload.ts
- Out of scope: BootScene wiring
- Out of scope: Phaser loading calls
- Out of scope: Changes to the manifest loader
- Preserve: Existing engine modules and the manifest loader behavior


## Technical constraints
- No node:fs import in the engine module, because the frontend bundles engine code
- Reuse the AssetManifest, SceneDef and EffectSpec types


## Definition of done
- Both functions are exported from game/src/engine/planPreload.ts
- The game typecheck passes


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · planPreload dedupes scene asset refs and reports unknown ones
nodes.body:
Context: SceneDef objects carry an optional asset, and dust effects carry an asset. Desired behavior: planPreload(scene, manifest) collects those refs, dedupes them in first-seen order, and splits them into ids to load and unknown ids. Expected result: a plan of the form { load, unknown }. Why: the scene must load each asset once and surface bad references.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given two objects that both use asset A, when planPreload runs, then load contains A exactly once.
- Given an object or dust effect with an id missing from the manifest, when planPreload runs, then unknown contains that id and load does not.
- Given a scene with no asset references, when planPreload runs, then load and unknown are both empty.


## Scope
- In scope: planPreload function and PreloadPlan type
- Out of scope: Loading the files in Phaser
- Preserve: SceneDef and manifest schema


## Technical constraints
- Pure function that takes the manifest as an argument


## Dependencies
- INT


## Definition of done
- planPreload is exported and returns a PreloadPlan


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · resolveTextureKey returns the fallback asset id for unknown ids
nodes.body:
Context: missing assets must not crash rendering. Desired behavior: resolveTextureKey(id, manifest, fallbackId) returns id when the manifest has it, and returns fallbackId when the id is unknown or undefined. Expected result: a texture key that is always safe to use. Why: the scene needs a safe texture key for objects whose asset is missing.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given an id present in the manifest, when resolveTextureKey runs, then it returns that id.
- Given an id absent from the manifest, when resolveTextureKey runs, then it returns the fallback id.
- Given an undefined id, when resolveTextureKey runs, then it returns the fallback id.


## Scope
- In scope: resolveTextureKey function
- Out of scope: Generating the fallback texture
- Preserve: FALLBACK_ASSET_ID value in the manifest loader


## Technical constraints
- The fallback id is passed in as a parameter, so the module does not import the node:fs-based loader


## Dependencies
- INT


## Definition of done
- resolveTextureKey is exported from game/src/engine/planPreload.ts


## Clarifying questions
- None

steps.action: Create the file. Export type PreloadPlan = { load: string[]; unknown: string[] }. Export function planPreload(scene: SceneDef, manifest: AssetManifest): PreloadPlan. Build refs from scene.objects[].asset (skip undefined), then from scene.effects entries whose type is 'dust' (their asset). Dedupe with a Set while keeping insertion order.
